note: Authored game dialogue for all nine scenes of Daniel 1. Reviewed and approved by Keith, 2026-07-29. Scene settings and cross-references come from content/daniel-1.refs.json. Lamplighter exits branch on all/some/none encounters engaged; PRD-12 wires the branch selection at runtime.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: There you are. Stay close to the lamp; the city is dark tonight, and something darker than night is on its way.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: This is where it all begins. See for yourself. I'll hold the light.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Walk around, talk to people. A few of them carry lanterns; they've been reading this story longer than anyone in the city, and what they know is worth hearing.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: The watchmen say the army stretches past the horizon. Whatever happens next, God isn't finished with us.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: My father named me "God is my judge." Not Babylon. I'm holding on to that tonight.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: My mother says we should pray. So I'm praying.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: Do you hear how quiet the streets are? A whole city holding its breath.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: I counted the watch-fires from the wall until I lost count.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: The elders keep arguing about what Egypt will do. Egypt feels very far away tonight.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: If the city falls, do you think God falls with it? Because I don't.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: I keep thinking about the prophets. Everyone said they were too gloomy.

beats.speaker: Nebuchadnezzar
beats.text: Egypt is not coming to save this city. No one is coming to save this city.

beats.speaker: Nebuchadnezzar
beats.text: When the gates open, bring me the best of it: the treasures and the sons. Babylon wastes nothing.

beats.speaker: Gatekeeper
beats.text: Forty years I've kept this gate. Never barred it against anything like this.

beats.speaker: A mother
beats.text: Inside, both of you, right now. The street is no place for children tonight.

beats.speaker: Soldier on the wall
beats.text: Stay off the wall. The watch changes at dusk.

beats.speaker: Market vendor
beats.text: No bread today. Maybe none tomorrow, either.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You listened to them all, the record and the warning both. So you already know the strangest thing about this siege: it didn't catch God by surprise. Come on. Let's see what this night brings.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You heard some of what this city has to say. There's always more, but no lamp burns forever. Come on. Let's see what this night brings.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: In a hurry? I understand; sieges do that to people. The lantern-carriers will keep their stories for another time. Come on. Let's see what this night brings.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: So the siege ended the way sieges usually do. Last night the gates opened.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: What happened next... well. See for yourself.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: The lantern-carriers in this courtyard have been reading too. If you find yourself asking how this could happen, they've been asking the same question a lot longer.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: They can carry the cups to Babylon. They can't carry God there; he's already everywhere they're going.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Watch the soldiers' faces. Even they handle those vessels carefully.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: I keep waiting for the sky to break open. It just stays quiet.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: We're on the list. All four of us. They're taking us with the treasure.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: My uncle served in that Temple his whole life. I can't even look at him today.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: "The Lord gave." That's what the scroll says. I'm still learning how to hear that.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Jeremiah said seventy years. That means there's an *end*, you know? I'm holding on to the end.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Pack light, they told us. As if anything we own is the heavy part.

beats.speaker: A Levite
beats.text: I polished those cups every festival since I was a boy.

beats.speaker: Babylonian officer
beats.text: Count every piece twice. The king wants an inventory, not a pile.

beats.speaker: Babylonian soldier
beats.text: Keep the line moving. These crates don't carry themselves.

beats.speaker: Onlooker in the crowd
beats.text: First the gold. What do they take next?

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: The song and the prophet agree, and now you've heard them both: this loss is discipline, not defeat. God gave, which means God is still in charge. Come on, the caravan is forming.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You've heard part of the answer, and it will keep. The rest is waiting in the songs and the scrolls. Come on, the caravan is forming.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Hard to look away, isn't it? Some things you just have to stand and watch. When you're ready to ask what it all means, the lanterns will still be lit. Come on, the caravan is forming.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Welcome to Babylon. A long road from Jerusalem, and the four of them walked every mile of it, same as you.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Marble where Jerusalem had stone, and a lamp in every hallway (though none of them, I notice, lights very far).

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: So what does an empire want with a crowd of young captives? See for yourself.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Quite a program, isn't it? The lantern-carriers have been here watching it take shape. If you're wondering what to make of it all, they're the ones to ask.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: They chose us for their program. God chose us first. I intend to remember the order.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Three years to learn everything Babylon knows. Fine. Let's see what they make of what we already know.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: We can learn their words without swallowing their gods. I think. I hope.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: Did you see the size of this place? Our whole street would fit in this courtyard.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: The library has ten thousand tablets, someone said. Ten thousand!

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: They keep calling us "the ones without defect." I feel plenty defective this morning.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: The food smells incredible. Honestly, that worries me more than the books do.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Three years. That's a long time to remember who you are, every single day.

beats.speaker: Ashpenaz
beats.text: Stand up straight. The king asked for young men with no flaws, quick in every kind of learning, and I intend to give him exactly that.

beats.speaker: Ashpenaz
beats.text: Three years, all paid for, eating from the king's own kitchen. There are princes in this city who'd envy what you're being handed.

beats.speaker: Palace scribe
beats.text: Name, age, city. Next.

beats.speaker: Court attendant
beats.text: The king's table serves forty dishes. You'll learn to like all of them.

beats.speaker: A fellow trainee
beats.text: Yesterday I was a captive. Today they're measuring me for palace clothes.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: A prophecy come true, a pattern to follow, and a warning about the king's table: you found all three. Hold on to them. Come on. The training is starting.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You've got part of the pattern now. The rest will keep; Babylon isn't going anywhere. Come on, the training is starting.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Dazzling, isn't it? Babylon means it to be. When the shine wears off, the lantern-carriers will still be here. Come on, the training is starting.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: They made the cut, all four of them. Three years in the king's program, starting today.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: First, though, there's a line at the registry hall. See what Babylon wants from them before the training even starts.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Watch the four of them at the front of the line. If you find yourself wondering what's really changing hands with those names, the lantern-carriers have been wondering longer.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Belteshazzar. That's what they'll call me now. They can write whatever they want on the tablet. God knows my name.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: A name is what someone calls you. It isn't who you are.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: Shadrach. I keep saying it and it still doesn't sound like me.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: My name meant "the LORD is gracious." I'm going to keep believing that, whatever they call me.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: Meshach now, apparently. My real name asks a question: "Who is like God?" No clay tablet changes the answer.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: They stamped it while I was still saying my old one.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Abednego. They can hand me a new name. They can't hand me a new God.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Say our real names when it's just us, all right? I don't want to forget the sound.

beats.speaker: Ashpenaz
beats.text: The scribe will read your new names. Learn to answer to them quickly; the king doesn't repeat himself.

beats.speaker: Ashpenaz
beats.text: A Babylonian name is a door, boys. Every door in this palace opens faster for one.

beats.speaker: Registry scribe
beats.text: New name, old name, city of birth. Press hard, the clay's drying.

beats.speaker: Trainee in line
beats.text: Took the scribe three tries to spell Belteshazzar.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: So now you know what a renaming tries to do, and why it doesn't get the final say. Joseph kept who he was. So can these four. Come on. The training is waiting.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You've heard part of what a name means here. The rest of the story will keep; names last a long time. Come on. The training is waiting.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Four names walked in, and four different names walked out. The lantern-carriers have thoughts about that, whenever you want to hear them. Come on. The training is waiting.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: New names, new clothes, new books. Babylon has been remaking those four from the outside in.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Tonight it's dinner. Smell that? The king's kitchen doesn't do anything halfway. See how the evening goes.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Keep an eye on Daniel and the official over there. The lantern-carriers are watching the same conversation; ask them what they see in it.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: The food itself isn't the point. The point is remembering whose I am, and some lines you have to draw while they're still small.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: I asked him kindly. You'd be surprised how far kindness goes, even in a palace.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: He asked the official politely. No speeches, no fists. Just steady.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: I was sure we'd be punished by now. Instead the man just looks... worried for us. Strange, isn't it?

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: We're with him. All four of us, or none.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: Everyone else thinks he's mad to risk the king's anger over dinner. I think he's the only one seeing clearly.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Vegetables and water. My mother would laugh, and then she'd be proud.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: It would be so easy to just eat. That's exactly why it matters that we don't.

beats.speaker: Ashpenaz
beats.text: I like you, Daniel, that's the trouble. If you four start looking pale and thin, it's my head the king takes. Do you understand that?

beats.speaker: Ashpenaz
beats.text: The king decided your menu himself. Nobody says no to the king's menu.

beats.speaker: Kitchen servant
beats.text: Roast, bread, wine, same as the king eats. Take a tray and move along.

beats.speaker: Trainee at the table
beats.text: The Judeans asked for vegetables. On purpose.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Favor from God, and a man freed from fear standing next to a man trapped by it. You saw both. Now let's see where Daniel's quiet line in the sand leads. Come on.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You've seen part of what's underneath this quiet little standoff. The rest will keep. Come on. Let's see where this goes.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Just a young man turning down a meal, or so it seems tonight. The lanterns will still be lit if you ever want to come back to it. Come on. Let's see where this goes.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Daniel asked his quiet question about the menu, and the official turned pale. That's where we left it.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: See what Daniel does next.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: The lantern-carriers can take you to other tables like this one: a desert, a palace, and a hungry evening. All three are worth the trip.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Ten days. Then look at us and judge for yourself. That's all we're asking.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: I didn't pick a fight. I proposed a test. There's a difference, and the attendant knew it.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: Day six. Honestly? I don't even miss it.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: The others keep waiting for us to break. It's become a kind of dinner theater.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: It's not about the food. It never was. It's about who we trust to keep us standing.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: Water tastes better when you know why you're drinking it.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: The attendant keeps checking our faces like we might faint mid-bite. We won't.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Ten days is nothing. Our people ate manna for forty years.

beats.speaker: The attendant
beats.text: Ten days. If this goes wrong, remember, it was your idea, not mine.

beats.speaker: The attendant
beats.text: I don't understand it. The ones eating roast and wine look tired, and the vegetable table is thriving. Explain that to me.

beats.speaker: Cook
beats.text: Four plates of vegetables again? You people are ruining my reputation.

beats.speaker: Trainee at the rich table
beats.text: More for the rest of us, I say.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: A desert, a palace, and a hungry evening: you visited all three. They all say the same thing, don't they? Real life doesn't come from the fancy plate. Come on. Three years of training go by fast.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You caught part of the lesson behind the vegetables. The rest keeps; that kind of lesson always does. Come on. Three years of training go by fast.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Ten days of vegetables, and the four of them are the healthiest young men in the palace. Make of that what you will, or ask a lantern-carrier what they make of it. Come on. Three years of training go by fast.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: The vegetables won. Ten days, and the king's own attendant couldn't argue with what he saw.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: That was dinner. The training itself is another story. See how the three years go.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Four star students, one question: why these four? Everyone in this library has a theory. The lantern-carriers have theirs; go hear it.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: I understood a dream last night. Really understood it, the way you understand a friend's voice. That doesn't come from tablets. God gave it.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: The more they teach us, the more I pray. Those two things are connected.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: Funny thing about Babylon's books: the more of them I read, the bigger God looks standing next to them.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: I answered a question today that our tutor couldn't. He just stared at me.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: The tutors come to us with questions now. It's the strangest thing.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: I actually like the astronomy. The stars belong to God anyway; Babylon just catalogued them.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Study hard, pray harder. That's the whole curriculum, if you ask me.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Three years ago I couldn't read a word of this language. Tell me that's not a gift.

beats.speaker: Chaldean tutor
beats.text: Twenty years teaching the king's trainees. I've never had to prepare this hard for my own students' questions.

beats.speaker: Library attendant
beats.text: Tablets back on the right shelf, please. The catalog took a lifetime.

beats.speaker: Student from another province
beats.text: I study all night and still place behind the Judeans. All four of them.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: A letter, a proverb, and an old story from Egypt, and all three put the credit in the same place. Wisdom is given, not manufactured. Come on. The training is nearly over.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You've heard some of where this wisdom comes from. The source isn't going anywhere. Come on. The training is nearly over.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Top of the class, all four of them. And the interesting question is why. The lantern-carriers love that question. Come on. The training is nearly over.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Three years, gone like a watch in the night. The training is over, and today every trainee stands in front of the king himself.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: I'd be nervous too. See how it goes for them.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Quite a turn: exiles standing at the top of the empire that dragged them here. The lantern-carriers watched the whole audience. Ask them what they saw.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Three years of training for one conversation. God was preparing us the whole time; the king only scheduled the meeting.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Whatever he asks, we answer honestly. Honest has worked so far.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: The king asked me about law and literature, and the answers were just... there. Given.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: I bowed to the king. My heart stayed standing; it belongs somewhere else.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: All that gold, and the guards, and the throne, and my knees held. God held them.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: Did you hear? None of the others came close. He kept all four of us.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: We walked in as captives. We walked out as the king's own advisors. Try explaining that without God.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Somewhere in Jerusalem there's a burned gate with my family's name near it. And now I stand here. What a strange road.

beats.speaker: Nebuchadnezzar
beats.text: I have interviewed every scholar this program produced. Where have these four been?

beats.speaker: Nebuchadnezzar
beats.text: Judah's God interests me. Judah's young men interest me more. They stay.

beats.speaker: Herald
beats.text: Next: the four from Judah. Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego.

beats.speaker: Palace guard
beats.text: Eyes forward. The king sees everything from up there.

beats.speaker: Courtier
beats.text: The king kept the Judeans past their hour. He never runs past the hour.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Skill honored, the lowly lifted, and wisdom no one could argue down: you found all three in one throne room. Come on. One scene left, and it's a good one.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You caught part of why this moment is bigger than a graduation. The rest will keep. Come on. One scene left.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Four exiles walk into the throne room and walk out as the king's advisors. The lantern-carriers saw the whole thing; they'd be glad to talk it over. Come on. One scene left.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: The four of them entered the king's service, and some time has passed. Life at court settled into, well, life at court.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: There's one more thing to see in this chapter, and it's worth seeing. Go ahead.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Ten times. Not a little better. Not competitive. Ten times, against the most celebrated experts the empire has.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: And that quiet last line: Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus. Sit with that one a moment. The lantern-carriers have been sitting with it for years.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Kings come and go. I've decided to stop being surprised by that.

beats.speaker: Daniel
beats.text: Ten times better, they say. I keep telling them the arithmetic isn't mine; wisdom belongs to God, and he's generous with it.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: They put our names in the court records today. Babylon writes us down; God wrote us down first.

beats.speaker: Hananiah
beats.text: Remember the night the city fell? I was sure the story was over. It was barely the first page.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: The magicians finally asked Daniel his secret. He told them. They didn't believe it could be that simple.

beats.speaker: Mishael
beats.text: We answer to the king now, and the king answers to God, whether he knows it yet or not.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Seventy years, Jeremiah said. We'll still be here, planted. Watch.

beats.speaker: Azariah
beats.text: Vegetables and water, and now this table. I laugh about it sometimes.

beats.speaker: Court magician
beats.text: We chart the stars all night. He asks his God and sleeps fine. I can't argue with the results.

beats.speaker: Palace messenger
beats.text: Message for Belteshazzar: the king's asking for him. Again.

beats.speaker: Junior scribe
beats.text: They say he'll outlast us all. The way things are going, I believe it.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Hollow experts, a wisdom that outgrows every teacher, and a believer who outlasts the empire itself: you've seen the whole picture now. That's chapter one. The story is just getting started.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: You've seen part of what "ten times better" really means. The rest will be here when you come back. That's chapter one. The story is just getting started.

beats.speaker: The Lamplighter
beats.text: Ten times better, and still standing when Cyrus takes the throne. The lantern-carriers can walk you through those lines whenever you like. That's chapter one. The story is just getting started.
